title: How Wond'rous Great, How Glorious Bright
description: How Wond'rous Great, How Glorious Bright in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 87, headed “The divine glories above our reason”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How won-d'rous great, how glo-rious bright Must our Cre-a-tor be, Who dwells a-midst the daz-zling light Of vast in-fin-i-ty!

lines: How wond'rous great, how glorious bright
Who dwells amidst the dazzling light
Fain would we see the blessed Three,
Our reason stretches all its wings,
But still how far beneath thy feet
Lord, here we bend our humble souls,
For the weak pinions of our mind
Can stretch a thought no more.
In vain the highest seraph tries
In humble notes our faith adores
While angels strain their nobler powers,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
